first_summary: Russia planned a roughly ten-day invasion; its tactical competence fell well short of expectations in the opening mechanized phase.
counter_summary: Case study of Ukrainian assaults through prepared Russian defences near Novodarivka and Rivnopil during the 2023 counteroffensive.

first_summary: Lessons list UAS and counter-UAS as required at all echelons and warn there is no sanctuary from observation and precision fires.
Report examines Russian electronic warfare as one of the combat functions Russia adapted, alongside engineers, artillery and armour.
counter_summary: A Ukrainian EW officer put the turning point at end-2024, when conventional jamming began to fail against new drone types.

first_summary: Responsive Russian fires were judged the greatest challenge to Ukrainian offensive operations.
Russian infantry moved from uniform battalion tactical groups to troops stratified into line, assault, specialised and disposable roles.
spread_summary: The third year was highly attritional: both sides focused on inflicting damage rather than achieving breakthroughs.

first_summary: Russia began fitting thermal camouflage to vehicles so tanks are harder to detect at range.

subtype_label: Separate drone service or elite drone center
first_summary: Ukraine announced a separate armed-forces branch for unmanned systems, covering aerial, ground and maritime drones.
spread_summary: Unmanned Systems Forces formally established with Col. Vadym Sukharevskyi as first commander.

first_summary: ISW assessed Russia was trying to mass-produce guided UMPB glide bombs and expand their use along the front, with claimed ranges of 80-90 km.
spread_summary: Russia increased its use of glide bombs against Ukrainian defensive positions during 2024.

first_summary: Argues UAVs should be treated as systems; software, sensors and radios need updating every 6-12 weeks to stay effective.
First reported Ukrainian ground assault using only robotic systems, without infantry, north of Kharkiv.
spread_summary: Khartiia reportedly cleared a strongpoint near Kupiansk with ground robots and strike drones and no infantry.

first_summary: ISW reported Russian forces increasingly using fiber-optic-controlled drones, which resist electronic warfare; mass use began in the Kursk campaign.
spread_summary: Fiber-optic FPV use spread along the front in 2025, used heavily by both sides.

first_summary: Ukraine fielded interceptor drones against Shahed-type long-range drones.
spread_summary: Ukrainian jamming and interceptors were assessed to have limited how widely Russia could field drones.

first_summary: ISW assessed Russia was preparing motorcycle assaults, likely to evade Ukrainian drones after heavy armored losses in 2024.
spread_summary: Russian MoD released motorcycle drill footage; ISW assessed Russia was likely developing doctrine for systematic offensive motorcycle use.

subtype_label: Targeting drone crews and their command posts
first_summary: Ukraine began a campaign to kill Rubikon drone operators no later than August 2025.

subtype_label: Drones loitering or perched on supply routes
first_summary: ISW cited 'waiter' drones perched along ground supply lines as a key Russian tool for restricting Ukrainian logistics around Pokrovsk.
Russian small groups infiltrated Pokrovsk, testing Ukraine's drone-based defence.

subtype_label: Drone-saturated zone behind the line of contact
first_summary: ISW assessed Ukraine's campaign against Rubikon operators had greatly degraded the unit's effectiveness by early 2026.

subtype_label: Strikes on drone units' bases and command
first_summary: Ukrainian forces struck a Rubikon base and a coordination center supporting Russian UAV units in Donetsk.
